stimuli.title: Nisha, Gita, Esha, Kiran, Pia, Meera, Lata, Ovi sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. For reference only, seats 1–8 run clockwise. For a centre-facing person, left is clockwise and right is anticlockwise.
stimuli.body:
Use all the following clues:
• Nisha occupies seat 3.
• Meera sits 3 place(s) to the left of Kiran.
• Ovi sits 3 place(s) to the left of Nisha.
• Kiran sits 3 place(s) to the left of Gita.
• Pia sits 5 place(s) to the left of Gita.

stimuli.body:

• Exactly 3 people sit between Gita and Riya.
• Exactly 4 people sit between Riya and Sana.
• Exactly 6 people sit between Esha and Farah.
• Exactly 1 person sits between Nisha and Sana.
• Exactly 2 people sit between Meera and Esha.

stimuli.title: Charu, Sana, Deepa, Lata, Kiran, Riya, Esha, Ovi occupy eight flats on floors 1 (bottom) to 4 (top). Each floor has Flat A to the west of Flat B. Each flat has one resident. For ordering only, count Floor 1 A, Floor 1 B, Floor 2 A, Floor 2 B, and so on.
stimuli.body:
Use all the following clues:
• Riya occupies floor 2, flat B.
• Kiran and Ovi live on the same floor.
• Deepa and Ovi occupy flats with different letters.
• Charu and Kiran occupy flats with different letters.
• The floor numbers of Sana and Esha differ by 2.
• The floor numbers of Charu and Ovi differ by 3.
• Sana and Riya occupy flats with the same letter on different floors.
• Riya and Esha live on the same floor.

stimuli.title: Farah, Nisha, Charu, Deepa, Jaya, Aditi, Sana, Lata attend interviews, one per slot, on 7 and 21 March, April, May and June. Slots run in chronological order.
stimuli.body:
Use all the following clues:
• Lata occupies June 21.
• Aditi attends in May.
• Charu attends on day 21 of a month.
• Jaya attends on day 7 of a month.
• Exactly 3 interview slots fall between the interviews of Farah and Lata.
• Exactly 6 interview slots fall between the interviews of Deepa and Lata.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few accounts are lockers. All lockers are deposits. No deposits is a cheques.
Conclusions:
I. Some accounts are not lockers.
II. No lockers is a cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few accounts are lockers. Some lockers are deposits. All deposits are cheques.
Conclusions:
I. All accounts are cheques.
II. No lockers is a cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some accounts are lockers. All lockers are deposits. No deposits is a cheques.
Conclusions:
I. Some accounts are deposits.
II. Some lockers are cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No accounts is a lockers. Some lockers are deposits. All deposits are cheques.
Conclusions:
I. All accounts are cheques.
II. Some cheques are lockers.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: X < P < S > V = U.
Conclusions: I. U > P   II. P ≥ V.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Either I or II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. Together the alternatives cover every permissible ordering, so either I or II follows.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
secure digital rural = ka mi lu
secure banking savings = vo ka to
digital banking growth = ze vo mi
rural savings growth = lu ze to
secure digital growth = ka mi ze
What is the code for “banking”?
questions.explanation: Answer: vo. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: secure = ka, digital = mi, rural = lu, banking = vo, savings = to, growth = ze.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 15 km east, turns left and walks 12 km, then turns left and walks 6 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 15. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 9 km along the initial direction and 12 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(9² + 12²) = 15 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 30 km east, turns right and walks 36 km, then turns right and walks 3 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 27 km along the initial direction and 36 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(27² + 36²) = 45 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 109 km south, turns right and walks 195 km, then turns right and walks 5 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 221. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 104 km along the initial direction and 195 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(104² + 195²) = 221 km.

questions.stem: E is the mother of F. H is the son of F. G is the father of F. How is H related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. G is a parent of F, and H is F’s son. Hence H is G’s grandchild.

questions.stem: D is the brother of F. F is the mother of A. E is the father of D and F. How is D related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. D is the brother of A’s mother F. Therefore D is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: A is the only daughter of C. C is the father of A. H is the son of A. D is the sister of C. How is C related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of A, and A is H’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 48 candidates, a candidate is 22th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 24. New front rank = 22+3 = 25. Back rank = 48 − 25 + 1 = 24.

questions.stem: In a queue of 51 candidates, a candidate is 9th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 39. New front rank = 9+4 = 13. Back rank = 51 − 13 + 1 = 39.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1850. It is marked above cost and sold at a 10% discount on marked price, earning 12% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2302.22. Selling price = 1850 × 112/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.9 = 2302.22.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 16 days and B in 24 days. They work together for 3 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need?
questions.explanation: Answer: 11. Use 48 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 48 − 3×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 240 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 16 km/h and stream speed is 4 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹22000 for 12 months. B invests ₹66000 for 9 months. Total profit is ₹101400. Find B’s share (₹).
questions.explanation: Answer: 70200. Capital-time ratio = 12 : 27. B’s share = total × 27/(39) = 70200.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹16000 at 20% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.explanation: Answer: 640. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 16000 × (20/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 90 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 18. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 18.

questions.stem: The average of 20 numbers is 66. One number, 78, is replaced and the average rises by 5. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 178. Total increases by 20 × 5. New number = 78 + 100.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 7 years, their combined age will be 74 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 14 = 74; x = 15, so father = 45.
